summary:
EARTHSONIC is an interactive NASA Earth Science sonification platform that transforms authentic Earth observation data into sound and visual experiences. It allows users to explore how our planet changes over time by listening to scientific measurements rather than relying only on charts and numbers.
The platform focuses on two important environmental indicators: global temperature anomalies and Arctic sea ice extent. By converting these measurements into carefully mapped audio parameters, EARTHSONIC makes long-term climate patterns easier to experience, understand, and compare.
Our vision is to make Earth science more accessible through an engaging combination of scientific data, visualization, and sound.
details:
EARTHSONIC – Listen to the Living Planet

Team Name: Binary Builder
Project Category: NASA Earth Science and Data Sonification

Problem Statement

Climate change is commonly communicated through scientific reports, graphs, maps, and numerical datasets. Although these methods are valuable, they can be difficult for general audiences to interpret, especially when trying to understand gradual changes over several decades.

Important environmental trends, such as rising global temperatures and declining Arctic sea ice, may appear as abstract numbers to people unfamiliar with scientific datasets.

EARTHSONIC addresses this communication challenge by introducing sonification, the process of converting scientific data into sound. It provides an additional way to perceive environmental changes and explore patterns through both hearing and visualization.

Proposed Solution

EARTHSONIC transforms verified scientific measurements into deterministic audio experiences. Each measurement is mapped to specific sound characteristics, including frequency, intensity, duration, and stereo positioning.

The platform currently supports two scientific datasets:

  1. Global Temperature Anomalies: Uses NASA GISTEMP Version 4 LOTI data, covering annual temperature anomalies from 1880 to 2023, relative to the 1951–1980 baseline.
  2. Arctic Sea Ice Extent: Uses the NSIDC Sea Ice Index Version 3, covering September sea ice extent observations from 1979 to 2023.

Users can explore these phenomena, select different years, listen to generated sound, inspect visualizations, and compare historical periods.

Key Features

1. Explore Earth

An interactive discovery page introducing the two supported environmental phenomena, their scientific datasets, and their sources.

2. Earth Studio

An interactive scientific workspace where users can select a phenomenon and explore changes across different years. The visualization and audio playback are designed to follow the selected scientific measurements.

3. Listen

A dedicated audio experience with playback controls, waveform visualization, and adjustable sound settings. Users can explore the generated audio and observe its changing parameters.

4. Compare

A historical comparison experience that allows users to examine different time periods, understand changes in temperature and sea ice, and compare their corresponding sound characteristics.

5. Scientific Information

The About section explains the data sources, scientific methodology, and the relationship between measurements and audio parameters.

Technology Stack

Frontend

  • React 19
  • TypeScript
  • Vite
  • Tailwind CSS
  • Web Audio API
  • HTML5 Canvas
  • Recharts

Backend

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • Pydantic
  • NumPy
  • Pandas
  • HTTPX

Scientific Data Sources

  • NASA GISTEMP Version 4
  • NSIDC Sea Ice Index Version 3
  • NASA Scientific Visualization Studio
  • NASA Global Imagery Browse Services

How It Works

The platform retrieves and processes scientific measurements from verified datasets. The backend validates, normalizes, and organizes the observations into chronological data points.

These measurements are then mapped to audio parameters using deterministic sonification rules. For example, increasing temperature anomalies produce higher pitches, while decreasing Arctic sea ice extent produces rising pitch. The frontend uses the Web Audio API to synthesize the resulting sound.

The visual interface presents the corresponding scientific information, allowing users to connect what they hear with the environmental changes represented by the data.

Reliability and Scientific Integrity

EARTHSONIC separates numerical scientific datasets from visualization assets to preserve data authenticity. NASA and NSIDC datasets provide the numerical measurements, while NASA SVS and GIBS are used for supporting visual content.

The backend includes data validation, caching, interpolation handling, and fallback mechanisms to improve reliability during demonstrations. The project includes automated backend tests and frontend production build verification.

Expected Impact

EARTHSONIC aims to make climate science more engaging, understandable, and accessible. By introducing sound as an additional way to interpret environmental data, the platform encourages users to explore long-term climate trends from a different perspective.

It demonstrates how scientific observations can become meaningful interactive experiences while maintaining a clear connection to their original measurements and sources.

EARTHSONIC: Listen to the Living Planet.
